title: Billing an Operator Surcharge to the Party on a Vacation Package
content:
Where the operator has notified a surcharge against a package among the Vacation Package Products, the charge for it is raised against the party as a whole and stands on that package's ledger. Raising it is the desk's own act: the agent performs it, and the party is billed by it.

## What raising the charge does

One charge raises a single surcharge line on the named package's ledger, for the amount given, in the currency the party is presented with, quoting the operator notice the charge answers. The line posts on the current business date, is charged against the party as a whole rather than any one traveller, and raises what the party owes on the package by that amount. The party sees the surcharge on the package statement from that moment.

## How it is raised

The agent-side tool `price_package_surcharge_8a2d0e07` is unlocked and then called by the agent.

## What must be given

| Given | What it is | Form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bundle_package_id` | the internal reference number of the vacation package the surcharge is billed to, read from the package record returned by the package lookup | an identifier |
| `surcharge_amount_usd` | the amount billed to the party for the surcharge; it is the total for the whole party rather than a figure per traveller | a USD amount with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the nearest cent, and never negative |
| `currency_charged` | the currency the party is presented with for this line; it records presentation only and never converts the amount given | an ISO 4217 currency code, 3 uppercase letters, in upper case and with no spaces |
| `notice_reference` | the operator notice reference quoted on the notice this surcharge answers, taken from that notice line on the package ledger | copied character for character, keeping its original wording, digits and punctuation, with no translation, normalisation, summarisation, addition or deletion |

## What comes back

A one-line confirmation string. It contains the reference number of the ledger line created, a string that begins with the letters bnx and an underscore, the amount posted in US dollars to two decimal places, and the package reference number it was billed to. A string of this shape means the surcharge line is now standing on the package; any other outcome means nothing posted.
